children: The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 0930 GMT on Tuesday:
** Tamarack Valley
and Headwater Exploration
will merge in an all-stock deal valued at C$10 billion ($7.25 billion), the companies said, creating the largest publicly traded producer focused on Alberta's Clearwater oil play.
** Poste Italiane
has raised the cash component of its takeover offer for Telecom Italia
, sweetening terms for shareholders as it seeks to secure control of Italy's former phone monopoly.

** Californian investment firm Platinum Equity is set to sell De Wave Group, maker of interiors for yachts and cruise ships, to Italian peer Renaissance Partners in a deal worth around €400 million ($465 million), a person close to the matter said.
** Rio Tinto
has agreed to acquire the Aurukun Bauxite Project in Western Cape York, Queensland from a joint venture between London-listed Glencore
and Mitsubishi Development, a company spokesperson said .
** Florida-based EverBank Financial has agreed to acquire WaFd
, a smaller bank in the Pacific Northwest, in a $3.9 billion reverse merger transaction, the companies said on Monday.

** Steve McGill said EQT’s agreement to acquire a majority stake in McGill and Partners marked a defining moment for the seven-year-old broker, giving it an “unprecedented” opportunity to accelerate growth while reinforcing the specialist boutique model on which the firm was built.

** French state-owned electric utility EDF is in talks to acquire electricity supplier So Energy, which is majority owned by Irish company ESB, a source with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Monday, confirming a media report from Sunday.
** Sweden has decided it will buy Lockheed Martin's
Himars artillery rocket system, Swedish Defence Minister Pal Jonson said on Monday.
** Australia's Santos
said on Monday it had acquired an additional 3.3% stake in the Papua LNG project from France's TotalEnergies
for $189 million, increasing its total interest in the venture to 21%.
** Australia's Ingenia Communities

turned down a A$1.94 billion ($1.40 billion) buyout offer on Monday from U.S.-based private equity firm Warburg Pincus, saying the bid undervalued the company and was not in shareholders' best interests.
** Dutch private equity firm Waterland plans to make an offer for British telecommunications company Gamma Communications
that exceeds the £1.08 billion ($1.38 billion) bid from Epiris, a British private equity firm, the Sunday Times reported.
